Definition.Name: Emergency hotfix rollout with shard-risk governance
Definition.Summary: Emergency delivery template for time-critical production remediation with explicit containment, rollback, customer communication, artifact-input, and approval discipline aligned to the current process architecture.
Definition.ValueStatement: Restores service or mitigates incident impact quickly without disguising rollback, data, or customer communication risk.
Definition.InterfaceContractSummary: Emergency software delivery spans production operations, customer communication, database safety, and release governance, so the process must keep those boundaries explicit.
Definition.GovernanceNotes: Time pressure never removes the need for explicit rollback ownership, communication ownership, typed emergency evidence, or explicit dependency joins.
Definition.ChangeSummary: Refreshed to use current first-class dependencies and artifact inputs for emergency approval instead of compressing them into legacy single-edge sequencing.
Definition.GovernancePolicySummary: Emergency release requires typed blast-radius analysis, focused QA proof, release approval, and explicit rollback trigger ownership.
Definition.ConstitutionRuleSummary: Command, communication, database safety, and rollout execution remain durable role contracts even if people on the rota change.
Definition.OperatingModeSummary: Emergency execution is allowed only inside a bounded release window with explicit rollback and communication obligations.
Definition.SimulationReadinessSummary: This scenario is intentionally rich enough for emergency simulation, incident replay, and canvas authoring validation.

Roles.Purpose: Drive containment and structured decision-making when time pressure and uncertainty are high.
Roles.StaffingIntent: A senior incident leader who can coordinate specialists, protect signal quality, and make time-sensitive trade-offs.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Crisis-flow owner for coordination, decision timing, and containment during active incidents.

Roles.Purpose: Provide the reliable platform path required to build, deploy, observe, and if necessary roll back changes safely.
Roles.StaffingIntent: A technical specialist in CI/CD, environments, infrastructure, and observability integration.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Environment and delivery-pipeline owner for build integrity, deployment mechanics, and operational guardrails.

Roles.Purpose: Own emergency database diagnostics, hotfix compatibility assessment, and rollback trigger definition.
Roles.StaffingIntent: A hands-on production database specialist for emergency change paths.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Specialist responder for shard, schema, and persistence hotfix risk.

Roles.Purpose: Challenge whether the delivered change is proven enough for its risk profile and make test evidence decision-ready for release governance.
Roles.StaffingIntent: A senior test leader able to shape strategy, select evidence depth, and identify where automation is not enough.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Quality owner for coverage depth, evidence quality, and release confidence.

Roles.Purpose: Decide whether the accumulated evidence is sufficient to expose the change to real users, data, and operational load.
Roles.StaffingIntent: A senior operational or governance authority who can accept release risk on behalf of the organization.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Final go-live decision owner for production promotion and rollback preparedness.

Roles.Purpose: Represent the customer communication path during release and incident work without allowing message drift from operational facts.
Roles.StaffingIntent: Customer communication owner for service-impacting release or incident lanes.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Customer communication owner for service-impacting release or incident lanes.

Steps.Title: Activate emergency bridge and classify severity
Steps.Subtitle: Command posture
Steps.Notes: Establish the incident bridge, initial severity, and named command boundaries before packaging a hotfix.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Active production signal, customer impact, and first-response telemetry.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Explicit command bridge with severity posture, responder roster, and immediate constraints.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Bridge activation log, severity declaration, and named responders.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Incident commander owns classification and decision pacing during the emergency window.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not begin emergency packaging while command ownership or severity framing is still implicit.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Command ownership may rebind across rota changes, but the command contract remains explicit.
Customer communication owner tracks external impact from the start.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Emergency bridge activation log
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for incident timeline, hotfix approval, and post-incident review.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must record activation time, severity, named responders, and first declared constraints.

Steps.Title: Assess blast radius and rollback constraints
Steps.Subtitle: Risk framing and bounded emergency scope
Steps.Notes: Determine which shards, data paths, tenants, and rollback constraints bound the emergency change.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Emergency bridge log, production telemetry, and known change hypotheses.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Explicit blast-radius assessment with rollback constraints and bounded emergency scope.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Impact map, rollback notes, and disallowed expansion paths.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Incident commander frames the boundary; platform and database owners challenge unsupported assumptions.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Pause immediately when the required fix grows into an unreviewable multi-area release.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Emergency boundary ownership stays with command.
Platform owner reviews operational fit of the proposed emergency boundary.
Database review is mandatory where shard state or tenant data is affected.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Blast-radius assessment
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for validation, release approval, and later incident review.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must identify impacted shards or services, rollback constraints, and forbidden scope expansion paths.

Steps.Title: Package emergency hotfix and rollback scripts
Steps.Subtitle: Controlled change assembly
Steps.Notes: Assemble the emergency patch, deployment instructions, and rollback scripts under one accountable engineer.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Blast-radius assessment, target change scope, and deployment constraints.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Hotfix package with rollout steps, rollback scripts, and changed-surface inventory.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Patch diff, deployment bundle, schema scripts, and operator checklist.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Platform engineer owns assembly but cannot expand scope beyond the approved emergency boundary.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Pause immediately when the required fix grows into an unreviewable multi-area release.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Emergency packaging remains attached to the platform-engineer role even if the individual changes.
Database review is mandatory for scripts that touch shard state or tenant data.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Emergency patch and rollback bundle
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for validation, release approval, and post-incident engineering review.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must link the exact patch, database scripts, rollback path, and operator checklist.

Steps.Title: Validate emergency fix in shadow environment
Steps.Subtitle: Fast but explicit regression gate
Steps.Notes: Run the emergency checklist against the hotfix bundle in a shadow or representative environment before release approval.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Emergency patch bundle, known blast radius, and incident reproduction notes.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Focused validation result with residual risks and unsupported cases.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Checklist output, shadow-environment notes, and residual-risk annotations.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: QA responder may block the rollout if the emergency evidence is too thin for the risk profile.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not convert the gate into a verbal approval; evidence still needs typed reviewable form.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Emergency QA ownership may move across the responder rota but the gate remains explicit.
Package owner reviews failures and unsupported coverage before approval.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Emergency validation evidence pack
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for emergency release approval and later correction of the emergency checklist.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must name validated flows, skipped checks, and residual risk that the approver must accept explicitly.

Steps.Title: Approve emergency release window
Steps.Subtitle: Explicit go / no-go and rollback trigger
Steps.Notes: Review the emergency evidence, rollback trigger, and customer communication plan before production rollout.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Validation evidence, rollback trigger, customer-impact status, and operator readiness.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Go / no-go decision with explicit rollback trigger and accountable owners.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Approval note, release window, fallback trigger, and outward-communication owner.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Release approver owns the emergency release decision and cannot waive missing evidence or unclear rollback control.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Reject the rollout when rollback conditions or customer-facing obligations are not explicit.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Emergency release approval remains attached to the role, not a specific operator.
Customer communication owner must review timing and outbound commitments before approval.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Emergency release approval record
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for audit, customer follow-up review, and future emergency policy tuning.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must name the approver, rollback trigger, communication owner, and residual risk owner.

Steps.Title: Execute emergency rollout and watch telemetry
Steps.Subtitle: Controlled production action
Steps.Notes: Roll out the patch inside the approved window while telemetry, shard locks, and customer communication remain actively managed.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Approved release record, deployment bundle, telemetry checkpoints, and customer message cadence.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Executed rollout with explicit telemetry outcome and rollback state.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Operator notes, telemetry checkpoints, rollback invocation if needed, and customer update timeline.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Platform engineer may execute only inside the approved window and rollback trigger boundaries.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Trigger rollback immediately when shard lock duration, tenant impact, or telemetry drift breaches the approved threshold.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Execution ownership remains with the platform-engineer role until rollout completes or fails.
Incident commander reviews telemetry and escalation timing throughout the rollout.
Database specialist remains an explicit fallback for rollback execution.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Emergency rollout and telemetry log
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for incident replay and emergency policy tuning.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must capture rollout timing, telemetry checkpoints, and any rollback invocation.

Steps.Title: Capture post-incident learning and corrective actions
Steps.Subtitle: Forensic replay and systemic follow-up
Steps.Notes: Turn the failed or recovered emergency path into explicit learning about detection, coordination, rollback, and architecture weaknesses.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Rollout outcome, telemetry record, customer communications, and command timeline.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Post-incident review with corrective actions, owner assignments, and simulation updates.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Timeline, contributing factors, missing controls, and next corrective actions.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Incident commander owns follow-up assignment while engineering and communications roles retain accountability for their control gaps.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not close the emergency process while corrective actions remain unnamed or unowned.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: The command role remains accountable until corrective actions have owners.
Engineering role reviews technical corrective actions.
Customer communication owner reviews trust and communication lessons.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Post-incident corrective action log
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for simulation packs, response playbook tuning, and recurring-incident analysis.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must capture missing controls, decision latency, and concrete corrective actions with owners.

Warnings: Detailed sidecar metadata remains in the process-template pack files.
